description:
FILED s536e (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) from a #4641 probe (scratch/s536e/pr/m5h.pl in the s536e worktree).  PRE-EXISTING: base c8886b61 and the s536e tree give the same answer.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    my @w; for my $i (1 .. 2) { foo(my $q = 0); push @w, sub { ++$q }; $w[-1]->() for 1 .. $i; sub peek { $q } }
    print join(",", map { $_->() } @w), " p=", peek(), "\n";
    sub foo { $_[0] }

perl:  2,3 p=2      (peek closes over the FIRST iteration's $q; the anon closures each over their own)
PCL:   3,4 p=4      (one shared cell: the veto keeps the package cell because the named sub uses the binding)

WHY: the file-level embedded-`my` veto (`_embedded_my_veto_names`, binder-keyed since s536e #4641) is RIGHT that the named sub needs a cell outside the `let`s; it models that by making the declaration THE cell for every execution.  perl's model: the named sub captures the pad entry of the first execution of its enclosing block; each later execution of the block allocates a new one ("Variable "$q" will not stay shared").

FIX DIRECTION (not designed): bind a fresh let per execution AND, on the first execution only, alias the named sub's cell to it (a once-flag around the publication) -- the statement-level `my` in a loop with a capturing named sub has the same shape; measure how often it occurs before designing (it warns in perl).

=== MEASURED (s537b, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-11) -- no code ===
CENSUS: scratch/s537b/loopsub-census.pl in the s537b worktree -- PPI + Pl::Binder (perl's pad model) over the s532c wide list (2,047 files: perl-tests 111, perl's t/ + core lib 1,360, the CPAN board cpan-tests 402, everyday 122, lib 52) + Pl/t/shapes 6; 55 perl t/ files PPI cannot read by name (utf8 sources) are not counted.  A row = a NAMED sub (not BEGIN & co.) inside a for / foreach / while / until BODY whose body captures (Binder::captures) a `my` of that body -- statement-level, embedded, or nested deeper in the body -- or the loop's own `for my $x` variable.

RESULT: ONE distinct site, in two copies of the same file:
    perl-tests/sort.t:832 = t/op/sort.t:832   `for(1,2) { my $failed = 0; sub rec { ... $failed = 1 if !defined $n; } rec(1); ok(!$failed, "sort from active sub") }`
a test written for the shape (its comment: "We run this twice, to make sure sort does not lower the ref count. See bug 71076").  Its OUTPUT is the same under perl and PCL (ok / ok: `$failed` is never set, `rec` returns early when sort calls it) -- probed, scratch/s537b/pr/m5c.pl.  ZERO sites outside test files (lib, the board's lib/ and t/, everyday: none).  No `loopvar` row at all.

PROBES (m5c.pl, perl -> main 3d524ad7 -> tree):
    this task's reproducer                             perl 2,3 p=2    PCL 3,4 p=4
    for my $i (1..3) { my $c = $i*10; sub first_c { $c } } print first_c()
                                                       perl 10         PCL 30   (the statement-level `my` too)
    the sort.t site                                    ok ok           ok ok

RECOMMENDATION (the reviewing session decides): a docs/not-supported.md entry, no code -- perl itself warns `Variable "$q" will not stay shared` for every such site, the census finds it in no real code, and the fix (a per-execution let plus a first-execution-only publication of the named sub's cell) would add a once-flag to every loop body that holds a named sub.  Proposed text:

    ## A named sub inside a loop body that captures a lexical of the body
    perl binds the named sub to the FIRST execution's variable ("Variable "$x" will
    not stay shared") and every later iteration gets a fresh one; PCL gives the
    sub and every iteration ONE variable (a package cell), so the loop's later
    iterations see the sub's writes and the sub sees theirs.
        for my $i (1 .. 3) { my $c = $i * 10; sub first_c { $c } }  print first_c()
        # perl 10, PCL 30
    Measured s537b (#4663): one site in the four populations, a test written for
    the shape (t/op/sort.t:832, whose output agrees).  perl warns at every such
    site; the idiom is a bug in the program.
subject: A NAMED sub inside a LOOP body that captures an expression-embedded `my` of the body shares ONE cell with every iteration (the file-level veto) -- perl binds the named sub to the FIRST iteration's variable ("will not stay shared"), later iterations get fresh ones (pre-existing)
